ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: What is the central or principal vein of a leaf called?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image contains a schematic diagram of two leaves. The leaf on the right has a thicker central leaf vein from near the petiole/base to the leaf tip, and thinner lateral veins branch from this main vein to both sides; the leaf on the left also shows veins extending outward from the central area. The question asks “what is the central or main vein of a leaf called”. According to leaf anatomical terminology, this central or principal vein is called the midrib.
